findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the 4-dimension variant
findings.body: Ruby has no method overloading. The new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` defined at line 149 replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately will now treat `max_height` as `opts`. That either raises when `opts[:...]` is called on an Integer, or produces wrong dimensions like "800" instead of "800x600".

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and the loop wastes work
findings.body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is never checked. If `convert` fails, for example on an unsupported format or SVG, the loop still runs up to 5 times and spawns a process each time. The upload then proceeds at its original size and is later rejected by the size validation.

findings.title: Stale tempfile size after in-place conversion
findings.body: `convert` rewrites the file at `tempfile.path` from a separate process while the Tempfile handle stays open. `tempfile.size` can report a stale or buffered size, so the loop condition may not reflect the new file. The same stale size is then passed to `Upload.create_for` at line 72.

findings.title: Client hardcodes 10MB limit for every file type, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb
findings.body: The client size check now uses a fixed 10MB for both images and attachments. Before, it read the per-type site setting. The server only downsizes images, so attachments larger than the configured attachment limit now pass the client check and fail on the server. Sites that allow more than 10MB are also capped incorrectly.

findings.title: API download limit hardcoded to 10MB
findings.body: URL downloads are now capped at a fixed 10MB for all types, regardless of settings. This should be configurable, or at least derived from the larger of the configured limits.
